settings.text:
For nearly a decade, I worked in the corporate world. My days were filled with meetings, work, travel, commutes, responsibilities and the constant feeling of having somewhere else to be.

I always knew I wanted to build something of my own, something where I could create, make decisions and bring an idea to life. Before EMBRAE, I explored a few different ideas. Skincare was the one that kept pulling me back, because it was something I genuinely cared about.

Living across different urban environments made me notice how differently my skin could feel from one place to another.

Humidity, heat, pollution, long commutes, air conditioning and stress each brought their own rhythm, and my skin experienced all of it.

I was already taking care of my skin. But finding products that actually felt right for my sensitive skin and for the realities of Indian weather wasn’t always easy. I tried different products and gradually built longer routines, thinking perhaps the answer was to do more. Too many products, and not always a clear idea of what each one was for.

But somewhere along the way, something felt wrong.
Skincare was supposed to be care. Why did it feel like another task?

That question stayed with me.

I started researching, learning about ingredients, formulation and how skincare products are created. I spent time understanding Indian skincare consumers and the realities of urban life. The more I learned, the clearer it became that I didn’t want to create just another skincare brand.

Somewhere in that learning, I came across Ectoin. It became an important part of how we approach formulation, and EMBRAE’s signature ingredient.

I wanted to create something I would genuinely want to use myself: simple, purposeful skincare that makes sense in real life.

That is where EMBRAE began.

The real work came next: speaking with manufacturers and vendors, reviewing samples, negotiating, and refining again and again. It is the first time I have built a brand from the ground up, and it has asked for a lot of learning, patience and courage, especially when things felt uncertain.

I want EMBRAE to be a brand that listens closely to the people who use it, keeps learning, never compromises on quality, and grows slowly and transparently. Something built to last. And if a customer tells me that EMBRAE made her skincare simpler, and helped with the problem she was facing, I will know we are on the right path.

For me, EMBRAE is about more than skincare. It’s about making space for yourself, even in the middle of everything life asks of you.

Because self-care doesn’t have to be complicated. Sometimes, it can simply mean taking a few minutes for yourself.

EMBRAE is rooted in the idea of embracing yourself through changing days, changing environments and everything life brings with it.

Because you don’t always need to do more. Sometimes, you just need a moment to care for yourself.

settings.heading: Skincare for real life.
settings.text: The simple, purposeful routine EMBRAE was built to be.
